# Long-term reanalysis-based energy yield of the Gulf of Saros offshore wind candidate area, Türkiye: sensitivity to reference period, grid node and wind data source

## Abstract

Türkiye published four candidate areas for offshore wind in May 2026. For the
Gulf of Saros area, this study asks what a public reanalysis indicates about
the long-term energy yield and how sensitive it is to often implicit choices.
Hourly ERA5 wind speeds for 1994–2024 at the grid node nearest the candidate
polygon were extrapolated to 105 m and converted hour by hour with a reference
9.5 MW power curve and assumed losses. The net specific yield is about 2.35
GWh MW⁻¹ yr⁻¹ (net capacity factor about 27 %), with a 90 % sampling
confidence interval of ±2.3 % for the 31-year mean. The two neighbouring ERA5
output nodes give +6.7 % and −8.5 %, with the same sign in every year. The
Global Wind Atlas indicates a mean wind speed about 12 % higher than ERA5 over
its mesoscale period, unresolvable from model data because the atlas is driven
by ERA5. The most recent 11 years give a yield 3.1 % higher than the 31-year
mean; this is the same size as the sampling uncertainty of an 11-year mean
(±3.8 %) and does not by itself establish a lasting change. The categories
differ in kind; they are not combined into one uncertainty interval. Screening
shows water depths below 62 m and an overlap of about 14 % with a Special
Environmental Protection Area. No result is validated against offshore
measurements. For narrow coastal areas, the reference period, grid node and
wind product should be reported and tested.

**Keywords:** offshore wind energy; ERA5 reanalysis; energy yield; capacity
factor; spatial representativeness; reference period; sensitivity analysis;
Global Wind Atlas; Gulf of Saros; Türkiye
